title: Preterm Labour and Threatened Preterm Birth

evidenceAudit.scope: Women with symptoms of preterm labour (intact membranes) between 22 and 37 weeks: diagnosis, tocolysis, corticosteroids, magnesium neuroprotection and preparation for preterm birth. Verified against NICE NG25 and the Saudi MOH OB/GYN Pocket Manual (preterm labour chapter); contraindications from FDA labels. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Preterm labour is regular painful contractions with cervical change before 37 completed weeks. Causes include infection/inflammation (chorioamnionitis), uterine over-distension (multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios), decidual haemorrhage (abruption), cervical insufficiency and stress pathways; prematurity is a leading cause of neonatal death.
keyMechanisms: Inflammation (cytokines, prostaglandins) ripens the cervix and triggers myometrial contractions — the basis for prostaglandin-synthetase inhibitors and oxytocin antagonists as tocolytics.
Tocolysis does not improve neonatal outcome itself; it buys up to 48 h for corticosteroids and in-utero transfer.
Antenatal corticosteroids accelerate surfactant production and lung maturation, reducing respiratory distress, intraventricular haemorrhage and necrotising enterocolitis.
Magnesium sulfate before birth under 30 weeks reduces cerebral palsy (neuroprotection).
Risk markers: previous preterm birth or mid-trimester loss, short cervix (25 mm or less at 16–24 weeks) — prevention with vaginal progesterone or cerclage (NICE).

symptoms: Regular painful contractions or tightenings; low back ache; pelvic pressure.
physicalSigns: Cervical dilatation more than 2 cm or effacement more than 50%, or change on serial examination (MOH).
Check fetal presentation and heart rate; signs of infection (fever, uterine tenderness).
redFlags: Advanced cervical dilatation — prepare for birth and neonatal team
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia — chorioamnionitis (no tocolysis)
Gestation below 30 weeks — magnesium neuroprotection and neonatal intensive care planning
precipitants: Previous preterm birth or mid-trimester loss; short cervix.
Multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, uterine anomaly, abruption.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Irregular, painless, no cervical change; cervical length above 15 mm.
Dysuria, loin pain — may trigger contractions.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and diagnose
actions: Senior obstetrician and neonatal team decide the plan; arrange in-utero transfer if needed.
29+6 weeks or less: treat as preterm labour. 30+0 weeks or more: cervical length (or fetal fibronectin) to decide.

clinicalManagement.title: Corticosteroids
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as preterm birth likely
actions: Offer at 24+0 to 33+6 weeks; consider at 34+0 to 35+6 weeks; discuss at 22+0 to 23+6 weeks (NICE).
Dexamethasone 12 mg IM every 12 h × 2 (MOH). One repeat course only if the first was more than 7 days ago and still under 34 weeks; never more than 2 courses.

clinicalManagement.title: Tocolysis (to allow steroids/transfer, up to 48 h)
actions: Nifedipine: offer at 26+0 to 33+6 weeks, consider at 24+0 to 25+6 weeks (NICE). MOH dose: 20 mg orally, then 10–20 mg every 6–8 h for up to 48 h.
If nifedipine contraindicated: atosiban 6.75 mg IV over 1 min, then 18 mg/h for 3 h, then 6 mg/h for up to 45 h (maximum 330 mg).
Do not use betamimetics (NICE) — oral terbutaline must not be used for tocolysis (FDA boxed warning). Indomethacin (MOH option at 24–32 weeks) carries fetal ductal and renal risks.
No tocolysis with chorioamnionitis, abruption, fetal compromise or advanced labour.

clinicalManagement.title: Magnesium sulfate neuroprotection
actions: Offer at 24+0 to 29+6 weeks; consider at 30+0 to 33+6 weeks; discuss at 23+0 to 23+6 weeks.
4 g IV over 15 min, then 1 g/h until birth or 24 h; monitor for toxicity at least every 4 h.

clinicalManagement.title: Intrapartum care
actions: GBS prophylaxis in labour: ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 h (MOH) — avoid other broad-spectrum antibiotics unless infection.
CTG or intermittent auscultation; delayed cord clamping per neonatal protocol.

medicationPlan.note: Tocolytic and steroid doses from the Saudi MOH OB/GYN manual; magnesium from NICE NG25; contraindications from FDA labels (atosiban is EU-licensed — check SFDA). NICE advises against betamimetics; MOH 2014 still lists ritodrine/terbutaline.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 24 to under 37 weeks; at least 2 painful contractions per 10 min plus dilatation above 2 cm or effacement above 50% or progressive change
Cervical length 15 mm or less, or fetal fibronectin above 50 ng/mL

values: Nifedipine; atosiban if contraindicated; no betamimetics
Indomethacin or nifedipine (24–32 wk); nifedipine, ritodrine or terbutaline (32–34 wk); atosiban
Neuroprotection 4 g + 1 g/h up to 24 h (under 30 weeks)
Cervical length 15 mm or fetal fibronectin 50 ng/mL

guidelineComparison.note: Follow NICE (newer evidence) for tocolytic choice and magnesium dosing; avoid oral terbutaline for tocolysis (FDA boxed warning).

learningObjectives: Diagnose preterm labour and give corticosteroids, tocolysis and magnesium neuroprotection appropriately.
keyPoints: Steroids 24–34 weeks: dexamethasone 12 mg IM ×2, 12 h apart.
Nifedipine first-line tocolysis; atosiban if contraindicated.
Magnesium 4 g + 1 g/h for birth under 30 weeks.
Cervical length 15 mm or fibronectin 50 ng/mL to decide at 30+ weeks.
No betamimetics; no tocolysis with infection or abruption.
